summary: This program defines a function named showWelcomeMessage() that prints a greeting, and the main method calls that function twice so the message appears two times.

lines.text: Calling a function is just writing its name followed by parentheses and a semicolon; control jumps to the function's body, runs it, and comes back to continue where it left off.
The second call reuses the same function rather than repeating the print statement, which is the whole point of writing a function: define the work once, use it as many times as you need.

This line is the function definition, and every piece of it matters: public is the modifier that controls who can call it, void is the return type saying it hands nothing back, and the empty parentheses mean it takes no parameters.

The function is defined after the closing brace of main, not inside it — functions sit side by side as members of the class, and Java finds showWelcomeMessage() regardless of whether it appears above or below main.
